name: SCOT (Digantara)

header.one_liner: SCOT is Digantara's space-situational-awareness satellite — described as among the world's first commercial SSA spacecraft — tracking resident space objects from orbit; it launched in January 2025.
header.indigenous_label: India-developed (Bengaluru); no audited indigenous percentage disclosed

at_a_glance.Claim: Among the world's first commercial space-situational-awareness satellites

what_it_is.prose: SCOT (Space Camera for Object Tracking) is a space-situational-awareness (SSA) satellite built by Digantara, a Bengaluru-based space-surveillance and intelligence startup. Launched on 14 January 2025 aboard SpaceX's Transporter-12 rideshare into a sun-synchronous orbit, SCOT is designed to detect and track resident space objects — including small debris reported down to around 5 cm — from orbit rather than from ground stations, giving weather-independent, higher-revisit tracking as part of a hybrid surveillance network. Digantara and press coverage describe it as among the world's first commercial SSA satellites and as India's first homegrown space-surveillance mission; the company reported commissioning and first imagery in early 2025. The capability supports orbital safety, collision avoidance and sovereign space-domain awareness, with obvious relevance to congested low Earth orbit and complex missions. This dossier records the launched, commissioned satellite and keeps sensor specifics and customer detail open pending primary disclosure.
